To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a numerical formulation for transferred potential analysis of grounding systems considering a layered soil model has been developed, which can be applied in the case of two-layer models.
we have developed a numerical approach to analyze transferred potentials in a grounding grid considering different soil models.
we have developed a new numerical technique based on BEM for the analysis of the transferred potentials in grounding grids considering a layered soil model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of numerical methods for the solution of the boundary value problem for the Laplace equation in two and three dimensions, with the objective of providing a powerful tool to solve the problems of the potential distribution in grounding systems and transferred earth potentials.

the development of an accurate and efficient numerical technique for the analysis of the transferred potentials due to the existence of metallic structures or conductive buried circuits in the surroundings of a grounding grid.

the development of a numerical formulation for calculating the earth potential in the vicinity of grounding grids due to the presence of metallic structures in the vicinity of the grounding grid and the soil stratification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the numerical formulation presented in this paper allows to accurately predict the transferred earth potentials in grounding systems due to buried conductors in the case of layered soils, which are very important for the design of electrical substations.
the use of the Boundary Element Method is very efficient and effective to analyze the transferred earth potentials in grounding grids.
the use of the proposed technique is recommended to perform a complete analysis of the potential distribution in the earth surface when the soil model is considered as a layered one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working on a new numerical technique to compute the potential distribution on earth surface when a ground fault occurs in an electrical substation.
the proposed technique allows to compute the potential distribution in the earth surface and in the grounding grid when an electrical fault occurs.
a general numerical formulation is presented for the analysis of the transferred potentials in earthing grids considering layered soil models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it provides a simple numerical approach that can be used for the analysis of the transferred potentials in earthing grids when layered soil models are considered.

the numerical formulation is able to compute the transferred potentials for any type of earth model and the results obtained for a two layer model are similar to those obtained by using a uniform soil model.
the numerical approach presented is a very useful tool for the analysis of the transferred potentials in grounding installations.
